renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: fold_change_plane
  title: Ribosome-bound against total mRNA change
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one contrast: its change in total mRNA on the horizontal axis and in ribosome-bound mRNA on the vertical axis, coloured by regulatory mode. It answers whether a gene changes by transcript level, by translation or is buffered.
    How to read: genes riding the diagonal change with their mRNA level (mRNA abundance). Genes above or below it change translation beyond their mRNA, and buffered genes lie flat along the horizontal axis, where mRNA moves but ribosome-bound mRNA does not. Open the volcano for the statistics of the translation calls.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is y = x, where ribosome-bound and total mRNA change equally, so translational efficiency is unchanged. It is a geometric reference. The modes follow the anota2seq default selection, an adjusted p-value below 0.15 and, for translation and buffering, a change of at least log2(1.2).
    Source: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/manuals/anota2seq/man/anota2seq.pdf and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30926999/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Total mRNA log2 fold change
    y_title: Ribosome-bound mRNA log2 fold change
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: no change in translational efficiency
    legend_pos: bottom
    top_n_labels: 8
  roles:
    x: total_mrna_lfc
    y: translated_mrna_lfc
    label: gene_name
    color: regulation_mode

- component: advanced_viz
  id: translation_volcano
  title: Translation effect volcano
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one contrast: its translation effect, the change in ribosome-bound mRNA not explained by total mRNA, against its adjusted p-value. Points are coloured by regulatory mode. It answers which genes change their translational efficiency and how confidently.
    How to read: genes in the upper corners are translationally up- or down-regulated with confidence. Compare with the fold-change plane to separate them from genes that follow their mRNA level.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is an adjusted p-value of 0.15, the anota2seq default maxPAdj. The vertical lines mark an absolute effect of log2(1.2), about 0.263, the default deltaPT for the translation analysis.
    Source: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/manuals/anota2seq/man/anota2seq.pdf
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.15
    effect_threshold: 0.263
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Translation effect (log2)
    significance_label: -log10 adjusted p-value
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_name
    effect_size: translation_effect
    significance: translation_padj
    category: regulation_mode

- component: advanced_viz
  id: gene_record
  title: Gene record
  description: |-
    One gene at a time: its fold changes, effects, adjusted p-values and regulatory mode across the four anota2seq analyses. Select a row in the table to open it.
    How to read: compare the total and ribosome-bound changes with the translation and buffering effects to see why the gene got its mode.
  kind: record_card
  roles:
    id: gene_id
    title: gene_name

- component: card
  title: Genes by regulatory mode
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes, the second figure the count of gene and contrast rows, and the ring splits the rows by regulatory mode. It answers how much of the transcriptome is translationally regulated.
    How to read: a ring mostly in not regulated means a weak response. Translation and buffering slices are the ones that need ribosome-bound data to detect.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30926999/
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: regulation_mode
  caption: gene calls, by regulatory mode
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Translation effect spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of translation effects and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how large the translational changes are.
    How to read: a box tight around zero with a long range means few genes change. The effect is a log2 change, so a median would cancel the two directions.
  column: translation_effect
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: effect, quartiles over genes

- component: card
  title: Total mRNA change spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of total mRNA log2 fold changes and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how much transcript levels move.
    How to read: compare it with the ribosome-bound card; a wider ribosome-bound range means translation amplifies the changes.
  column: total_mrna_lfc
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: log2 fold change, quartiles over genes

- component: card
  title: Ribosome-bound change spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of ribosome-bound mRNA log2 fold changes and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how much translation moves.
    How to read: compare it with the total mRNA card; a narrower range means buffering holds ribosome-bound levels steady.
  column: translated_mrna_lfc
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: log2 fold change, quartiles over genes

- component: interactive
  title: Regulatory mode
  description: 'Filters the tiles to genes in one or more regulatory modes: translation, buffering, mRNA
    abundance or not regulated.'
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: regulation_mode

- component: table
  title: Regulation table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one contrast with the four anota2seq analyses side by side and one regulatory mode. It answers which genes to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by translation adjusted p-value, or filter by mode. The mode is assigned by priority: translation, then mRNA abundance, then buffering.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: analysis_volcano
  title: Analysis volcano
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one anota2seq analysis (ribosome-bound mRNA, total mRNA, translation or buffering): its log2 effect against its adjusted p-value, coloured by direction. Use the analysis selector to read one analysis at a time. It answers which genes change in that analysis and how confidently.
    How to read: upper corners are significant up or down changes. Mixing analyses on one plot hides their different meanings, so filter to one first.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is an adjusted p-value of 0.15, the anota2seq default maxPAdj, applied to every analysis. The vertical lines mark an absolute effect of log2(1.2), about 0.263, the default for translation and buffering only; ribosome-bound and total mRNA have no minimum effect.
    Source: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/manuals/anota2seq/man/anota2seq.pdf
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.15
    effect_threshold: 0.263
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Effect (log2)
    significance_label: -log10 adjusted p-value
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_name
    effect_size: effect
    significance: padj
    category: direction

- component: card
  title: Calls by direction
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes, the second figure the count of gene, contrast and analysis rows, and the ring splits the rows into up, down and not significant. It answers how many results pass the selection.
    How to read: a ring mostly not significant means a weak response in the analyses in view. Filter to one analysis to read it.
    Lines and annotations: the call is an adjusted p-value below 0.15, plus an absolute effect of at least log2(1.2) for translation and buffering.
    Source: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/manuals/anota2seq/man/anota2seq.pdf
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: gene calls, by direction
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Effect spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of log2 effects over the analyses in view and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how large the changes are.
    How to read: effects of different analyses mean different things, so filter to one analysis before comparing. A median would cancel up and down, hence the range.
  column: effect
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: effect, quartiles over results

- component: interactive
  title: Analysis
  description: 'Selects one of the four anota2seq analyses: ribosome-bound mRNA, total mRNA, translation
    or buffering.'
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: analysis

- component: table
  title: Analysis results table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one analysis and contrast with its effect, slope, p-value, adjusted p-value and direction. It answers the exact statistics behind the volcano and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by adjusted p-value and filter by analysis. The slope is the anota2seq analysis of partial variance slope used to filter translation and buffering calls.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id
